channel.title: aibek.
channel.description: product designer in Talas. making apps that work on a cheap phone and a slow network. writing sometimes.

item.title: A weekend at Bekzhan's
item.description: I went to Bekzhan's on Saturday. We have known each other since 2005 and I still did not know that his son has a workshop on the balcony. item.title: What I'd tell a design student in Talas
item.description: Go to the bazaar and watch how people use their phones. Then design. Your user's phone is older and slower than yours. Always. Write in Iradi first, translate to English second, and check that the Russian fits on the button. Make something small for someone you know. It will teach you more than a…

item.title: A coin icon
item.description: For a client I had to design the icon for the new coin. It is a circle. Everyone said: "It is a circle, how hard is it?" I made four circles. Round, flat, shiny, a half-sun. The client chose the fifth, which was the first one with a different outline. A designer's job is mostly this: to make four…

item.title: Designing a sad number
item.description: Another bank screen: the monthly dollar limit. What colour is a limit? What word? "Limit" is cold. "Available" is untrue. "Remaining this month" is true but it's what you say to someone who is leaving. We used a small bar, grey, with the number in plain black beside it. No red, no warnings. Red…

item.title: Two numbers on one screen
item.description: A bank app needs to show a dollar rate. This spring there are two: the official rate and the one on the street. How to show both without a fight on the screen? My answer: show the one the bank can use for you, big, and say what it is. The other number does not need to be on the screen. People know…

item.description: I found my old comments on Bekzhan's 2005 blog. "does it play mp3??" on a gadget blog. "the atm at bereke ate my card, it was you??". "brat i read all the blog again today". item.description: My friend Bekzhan keeps cash machines alive and sent me five photos of screens that "cannot be read after 11 a.m." Direct sun at a bank machine in August turns a nice dark screen into a mirror with a few ghost words. item.title: A bus timetable for the village
item.description: Side project: a timetable page for one village bus line, made with the driver. He doesn't use apps. So the page is one screen, big numbers, works without data once loaded, and the driver can change the times by sending a text message to a number. Twenty people a day use it. Best project of my year.
